answer: A concurrency audit makes each key prove its own live compute. At a random second each epoch, the onyx round fires: every key gets an ivory prompt seeded from its own address and must return a 200-word answer a verifier model accepts within 20 seconds. Replying on time keeps the key's lotus, its full reward multiplier; a late or missing reply halves it. One GPU finishes only one such answer in 20 seconds, so keys sharing hardware fail, and since the second is unknown, capacity stays reserved all epoch. Attacker pays: 1,000 fakes need 1,000 GPUs for 6 hours at $2/hour, $12,000 this epoch.
